relevance_note: Case report of a German man with fish eye syndrome who is "a compound heterozygote for the Thr123 → Ile mutation and a previously undescribed Thr347 → Met mutation in the LCAT gene", plus his heterozygous daughter.
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; a short Python script assembled the JSON and sliced table-row spans (checked against the tables). In scope: the proband ('patient', rule 5; the daughter is a relative, 'daughter of patient') and the three previously reported Swedish fish eye disease patients shown as data columns 4-6 of Table I (column headers '*1899;t', 'Sweden *1908;t', '*1914; t'; data columns counted from the left after the row-label column: 1 controls, 2 proband, 3 daughter). The *1908 and *1914 Swedish patients reappear as Table II data columns 4 and 5 ('Sweden - *1908;t', 'Sweden - *1914;t') and were matched by birth year and country; their Table I labels are used. The Swedish patients' genetic defect is stated as not reported, so they have no variant rows. Their vital status 'deceased' reads the OCR 't' in the column header as the dagger the legend defines as deceased. Their low HDL, hypertriglyceridemia, reduced HDL CE % and reduced LCAT activity were read from Table I/II values against the control range printed in the same row; group-level features (corneal opacification, 90% HDL CE reduction, normal CER and total CE, no premature atherosclerosis/anemia/renal disease) come from statements naming the Swedish patients ('the subjects with fish eye disease' in the Introduction refers to the three Swedish subjects of the preceding sentences). 'No premature atherosclerosis' was not used to exclude the broader checklist item atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease; 'no renal disease' was used to exclude only 'chronic kidney disease or renal failure', not specific renal signs or histology. Out of scope: the Canadian patient (only 'resembling fish eye disease', ref 13), the four German/Dutch Thr123Ile patients (refs 16, 17; group-level only), and the apo A-I frameshift subject (ref 42, other gene); variants listed in Fig. 4/Table III from classic LCAT deficiency are not tied to individuals. Checklist 'reduced cholesteryl ester fraction' left not reported for all: the paper reports a reduced HDL cholesteryl ester fraction but a near-normal total plasma cholesteryl ester fraction, and the checklist item does not say which compartment; both are recorded as phenotypic_features. Daughter: 'no abnormalities in lipoprotein profile' recorded as an excluded whole-profile finding only (D-27), not used to exclude specific checklist lipid items; 'asymptomatic' not converted into exclusions. Daughter tested normal at the Thr347 locus ('the DNA sequence of exon 6 was identical to the normal allele'), so she has no Thr347Met row. Variant type 'missense' is recorded from the stated amino-acid substitutions (threonine to isoleucine / methionine). Pathogenicity for the proband's variants is the authors' 'class II' classification; it is not repeated for the daughter's row. Functional evidence is plasma enzyme activity in the carriers, not an in-vitro assay of each variant. The proband's age (66 yr) is recorded as age at last evaluation; he was born in 1925, daughter born 1957 (34-yr-old). Contradictions/oddities: abstract gives control LCAT activity 25.1–27.9 while Table II prints 25.1-27.5; Table II prints CER in VLDL/LDL-depleted plasma for the proband as '[61' while the text says 12% of CER on HDL; the lipoprotein electrophoresis sentence is truncated by the conversion; the abstract says HDL cholesterol 7.7 mg/dl and Table I prints 8.
